reason: Large-vessel immune vasculitis defines the primary axes; frequent skin ulcers and arthritis support the involved axes. Pharyngeal-arch ancestry does not establish airway disease.
Sweat-gland and hair abnormalities define this subtype. Hypodontia occurs in 2/10 patients, below the involvement threshold; gastrointestinal involvement is not established.
The ampullary origin supports hepatic and gastrointestinal axes. Small-cell morphology does not imply pulmonary origin, and neuroendocrine differentiation does not itself establish endocrine disease.
Neuropathy defines the disease. Frequent fixed contractures and foot deformities support musculoskeletal involvement; frequent vocal-cord paresis establishes persistent laryngeal dysfunction.
The Bardet-Biedl phenotype supports defining retinal, metabolic and skeletal abnormalities, with renal involvement around 30-50%. The four-axis cap reasonably excludes neurodevelopmental involvement.
Remove otologic, gastrointestinal and cardiovascular: findings reported in 1/1 assessed patients do not establish prevalence of at least 30% or major diagnostic criteria across this syndrome.

corrected.basis: STAG2 neurodevelopmental syndrome. Ear defects, cleft palate, VSD and scoliosis are single-patient observations; their population frequencies are not established.

reason: Pituitary endocrine origin defines the primary axis. Frequent progressive visual loss supports ocular involvement, and frequent bone loss supports musculoskeletal involvement. Headache does not establish neurologic damage.
Pancreatic inflammation establishes gastrointestinal disease. Inflammation alone does not establish an immune-mediated mechanism; endocrine injury is not defining or common across this umbrella.

Remove hepatic and renal: glycogenosis and Fanconi dysfunction characterize rare HNF4A variants, not the broader condition. Remove neurologic: lasting injury in at least 30% is not established; pooled HPO frequencies overgeneralize syndromic presentations.

corrected.basis: Endocrine hyperinsulinism; hepatic glycogenosis/Fanconi are rare variant-specific features. Common lasting neurologic injury is not established; later MODY is a separate disease.
